guard: setup seeds personas into the catalog resolved for the selected mesh
why: TWO MUTATIONS cover the destination and the folded resolver-to-writer wiring. The first still
returned target still names it, but dir is silently replaced with the cwd-derived catalog. That
is the precise state in which setup reports success while a following spawn cannot find the file.
The substitution is compile-clean and occurs after resolveMeshTarget succeeds, so the mutation
cannot be killed merely because target selection stopped working. The first alpha destination
cell must redden by name; an unrelated throw or later parse failure does not count.
The second mutation removes the write from seedDefaultForSetup, the helper production setup and
the smoke both call. This closes the prior seam-only gap: resolution can remain correct while the
shipped wiring never hands that destination to the persona writer. The named write cell kills it.

mutations.name: setup resolves a mesh but seeds the cwd catalog
mutations.expectRed: alpha: the destination is the RESOLVED MESH's catalog, not the cwd's
mutations.cell: alpha: the destination is the RESOLVED MESH's catalog, not the cwd's
mutations.note: This changes only the chosen write directory, retains the resolved mesh metadata, and typechecks before the smoke runs.

mutations.name: setup resolves and announces a destination but never passes it to the shipped persona writer
mutations.expectRed: the seed actually wrote the file
mutations.cell: the seed actually wrote the file
mutations.note: This compile-clean mutation breaks production's resolver-to-writer helper rather than the smoke's arithmetic or a restated rule.
